name: Hydro turbine generator
summary: A water turbine driving a generator, used for mini and micro hydro sources within microgrids and remote supplies.
description: A hydro turbine generator converts water flow and head into electrical power through a Pelton, Francis, Kaplan or crossflow turbine driving a synchronous or induction generator. In microgrids, small hydro is valuable because it is dispatchable within the limits of the water available and supplies real rotating inertia.

Drawings show a turbine element on the shaft line to the generator circle, sometimes with a governor or a dump-load controller attached. Very small run-of-river units often regulate frequency by diverting surplus power to a ballast load rather than adjusting water flow, so the dump load may appear beside the generator.

The symbol does not state head, flow, runaway speed or whether the unit can operate isolated. Penstock and water-hammer constraints limit how quickly load can change, which is not visible on the electrical drawing.
readingNotes: A ballast or dump load beside a small hydro set indicates electronic load control instead of a mechanical governor.
Check whether the generator is synchronous or induction.
drawingChecklist: State turbine type, head and flow.
distinction: A hydro unit is driven by water; its control differs from a thermal genset because load changes are limited by penstock dynamics.
